title: A.K. Gopalan v. State of Madras

content.caseIdentity: A.K. Gopalan v. State of Madras, AIR 1950 SC 27; 1950 SCR 88
content.facts: Challenge to preventive detention under the Preventive Detention Act, 1950, raising the meaning of procedure established by law in Article 21 and the relationship among Articles 14, 19 and 21.
questionsBeforeCourt: Whether procedure established by law under Article 21 requires more than a procedure enacted by a competent legislature
Whether Articles 19 and 21 must be read together in testing a detention law
content.holding: The Court upheld a narrower, compartmentalised reading associated with Article 21 as satisfied by procedure enacted by law.
content.ratioDecidendi: Historically, Article 21 was read as requiring procedure established by enacted law, with Fundamental Rights analysed in relative isolation — later superseded in approach by Maneka Gandhi.
content.presentLegalPosition: Gopalan remains historically important. Controlling modern reading is Maneka Gandhi (1978) 1 SCC 248.
content.practicalSignificance: Use Gopalan as historical contrast when teaching Maneka and the golden triangle.
content.relevance: A.K. Gopalan is a foundational early Article 21 and preventive-detention decision. It is especially relevant for understanding the pre-Maneka approach to the relationship among Articles 14, 19, 21 and 22 and the later shift toward an integrated reading of Fundamental Rights.
